lina: Quick sync — I noticed an uptick in error rates when request logging is enabled for the new routing rules. Can we decide what to log at the edge vs. in the control plane?
omar: Good catch. Are these errors coming from sampling overload or payload size/timeouts?
leo: Mostly from large payloads hitting the scrubber step, some requests time out waiting for redaction.
anita: We need logs for quota enforcement and billing; but we also must avoid PII leak. Proposal: edge logs only metadata + hashed user_id, control plane keeps full payloads but encrypted and access-audited.
lina: That would reduce egress and keep latency lower. How do we handle embeddings and prompt context which can contain PII?
omar: Two ideas — prefix-based scrubber at edge that redacts anything matching PII regexes, or sample full payloads at 1% for QA and keep deterministic hashing for lookups.
leo: Regexes are brittle. We have to support structured redaction rules per route (e.g., chat vs. completion vs. embedding). 
anita: Can console let teams opt into "debug-raw" for short windows with approval? We should make it an explicit canary flow with reason and TTL.
lina: +1 to TTL breakglass. But we need to ensure quotas still work if payloads are redacted — token counting must be done before redaction.
omar: Right. Tokenization happens in the runtime; edge reports token_count as an integer to billing service. The raw tokens never have to leave the runtime if we only send counts.
leo: Ops concern: sampling needs to be route-aware. If we sample uniformly 1% we might miss rare failure modes on low-volume routes. Suggest stratified sampling: min 1 per 1k requests per route, plus 0.1% global.
anita: UX for console: show sampled vs unsampled rates, plus an override to increase sampling for a route over a time window. Also surface PII redaction coverage metric (how many matches removed vs total).
lina: Can we do local KV-cache of redaction patterns per region to avoid cross-region lookups? That would cut latency.
omar: Yes — publish approved pattern bundles to edge nodes. They should be signed; edge verifies signature before applying. Bundles versioned and canaryed.
leo: Implementation note: keep a small fast path which only applies the common safe list and a slow path that calls into heavy NLP scrubber when confidence < 0.7. Fast path = regex + token mask, slow path = model-based redaction.
anita: Compliance: we need an audit table that records who accessed raw payloads, why, and associated console approval id. That table must be immutable and retained per policy.
lina: What about telemetry volume? If we keep too many deltas for redaction operations it will blow up our observability costs. Maybe store counts and hashes rather than full diffs.
omar: Agreed. Telemetry items: route, redaction_count, token_count, sampling_decision, scrubber_version, run_time_ms. No raw content.
leo: Edge default config suggestion: sampling=0.1% global, stratified-min=1/1000 per route, scrubber_mode=fast, allow_debug_raw=false. Teams can request higher sampling or debug via console and approvals.
anita: We'll add a console flow: Request -> Approver -> TTL auto-expiry -> Audit entry. Also an alert if debug_raw used more than X times in 24h.
lina: For rollouts, we should A/B the scrubber: canary 5% of traffic to model-based scrubber and monitor latency + redaction delta. If delta > threshold revert.
omar: Add fallback: if scrubber slow or error, fallback to conservative redaction (strip all user-sent text fields) and continue. Log a non-sensitive error event.
leo: Example config snippet:```json
{
  "sampling": "0.001",
  "stratified_min": "0.001",
  "scrubber_mode": "fast",
  "debug_raw_allowed": "false",
  "bundle_version": "2026-03-01-v3"
}
```
anita: Who owns the policy doc? @lina to draft initial RFC, @omar to add infra constraints, @leo for runtime implementation notes, I'll handle console/approval UX.
sre-bot: Incident alert suppressed: scrubber-fallback triggered 3 times in last 10m on us-west-2 — currently routing 95% through fast path.
lina: Thanks bot. Action items: 1) Lina RFC draft by EOD Friday, 2) Omar provide signed bundle mechanism + schema, 3) Leo prototype fast/slow path switch, 4) Anita wire console approval flow.
omar: I'll sketch the signing scheme and a backwards-compatible bundle format.
leo: I'll add telemetry metrics to the runtime export.
anita: I'll mock console screens and error states.
lina: Cool. One more: make sure token_count computation is consistent across runtime versions — add versioned tokenizer id to telemetry.
omar: Noted. Closing for now, will ping when RFC link is up. :thumbsup:
